svg.title: Two organisations, and the three tenants that serve them
svg.desc: Above the deployment, two kinds of thing that are not inside it. Applications ask the store: the clinic's own application over FHIR, and a host that embeds the store in its own JVM, each carrying a token from that tenant's own issuer. Participants are offered work: a bench instrument behind a router and a supplier's own system elsewhere, each holding an enrolment and taking work it asked for. Inside one node are five tenants. Three supply: a zone holding which brokers authenticate and which identifiers prove, a face root holding a FHIR version's structures, searches, value sets and codes, and a managing tenant holding what this deployment was told to serve. Two are served: the clinic and the laboratory, each with its own issuer, keys and people. What the zone and the face root hold moves down one way, only where the tenant below declared it, read-only where it lands and stamped with where it came from, and never carrying a person. Beneath, five databases, one per tenant. Nothing reads another tenant's records, for anybody, the operator included.

g.text: TWO ORGANISATIONS, AND THE THREE TENANTS THAT SERVE THEM
the clinic's own application, over FHIR
a host that embeds the store in its JVM
a bench instrument, behind a router
a token from that tenant's own issuer
an enrolment, and work it asked for
one node — one process, one port
one way, and only what the tenant below declared it takes — read-only where it lands,
stamped with where it came from, and never a person
its own issuer and keys, its own people,
its own issuer and keys, its own people,
a connection handed to each, and never a credential the operator holds
what is not drawn because it does not exist: a read of another tenant's records, for
anybody including the operator; a broker beside the databases; a call from the node out
